\caption[Robustness of the survey verdicts]{Robustness checks of the survey, all exploratory (deviations 21, 27 and 29 of \file{study/PROTOCOL.md}): they say whether a verdict is fragile, without changing any. Columns: the four criteria that changed (Q5, Y9, X7, X2) and the two whose interval avoids zero without passing Holm (Q6, Y12). Gaps in points (classical RL 2026 minus our reading of 2018), 95\% Newcombe interval, Fisher test, Holm over the criterion's grid family as in the main comparison. (a1) classical RL 2026 split by provenance (first draw with no title screen, A3 queue with the screen), then Fisher $p$ between the two provenances within 2026; (a2) Fisher $p$ between 2026 papers read on arXiv (45) and on a conference site (5), a cut too unbalanced to settle anything (deviation 21 c); (a3) Cochran-Mantel-Haenszel test stratified by conference (Haldane correction); (a4) comparison redone without each primary reader in turn: range of the gaps and lowest lower bound; a criterion is fragile when the gap changes sign or the interval contains zero with at least 35 papers on each side. Bottom part: without the thirteen papers read partly by \texttt{claude-opus-5} (deviation 29); with the 10 `no' decisions a blind arbiter turned after the keyword search, then with the 24 decisions judged doubtful as well, out of 377 `no' decisions examined (deviation 27). \textbf{In bold}, gaps whose interval excludes zero and $p$ below 0.05 (except the homogeneity $p$ of (a1) and (a2), where a high $p$ is expected). The thesis `heeded where it cost little' is rejected by the blind test (b): Spearman correlation between the observed gap and the median cost scored by three raters +0.16 (permutation $p$ 0.52), with the risk −0.04 ($p$ = 0.89). Sources: \file{study/robustness.json}, \file{study/extension\_stats\_sans\_opus5.json}, \file{study/extension\_stats\_falsify\_turned.json}, \file{study/extension\_stats\_falsify\_bound.json}, \file{study/falsify\_no.json}.}
